lines.p1: The browser receives H T M L as raw bytes. It decodes them into characters, then into tokens.
lines.p2: Tokens become nodes, and the nodes form a tree: the D O M.
lines.c1: C S S is parsed the same way, into the C S S O M, a tree of style rules.
lines.c2: It blocks rendering: the browser waits for the styles before it paints anything.
lines.r1: The D O M and the C S S O M combine into the render tree, which holds only what is visible.
lines.r2: The head, and anything with display none, is left out.
lines.l1: Layout works out the size and position of every box, in pixels.
lines.l2: Resize the window, and the browser has to lay everything out again.
lines.pa1: Paint turns boxes into pixels: text, colors, borders and images, drawn into layers.
lines.pa2: The G P U then composites the layers into the final frame on your screen.
lines.j1: Java Script can change the D O M or the styles, and the pipeline runs again from that step.
lines.j2: Changing transform or opacity only needs compositing, so it is cheap and smooth.
lines.outro: H T M L and C S S become trees, trees become boxes, and boxes become pixels. That is how a browser renders a page.
